sections.title: Extreme places

q.prompt: Which word means “a very dry place with little rain”?
q.reason: “desert” means a very dry place with little rain.

options.fb: “ocean” means a very large area of sea.
“volcano” means a mountain that can send out hot rock and ash.

captions: Hello, and welcome to Atomic English, Stage 4. In this lesson: Extreme places.
Use superlatives to compare three or more things.
Here are some new words. Desert. A very dry place with little rain. Volcano.
A mountain that can send out hot rock and ash. Ocean. A very large area of sea.
Listen and say them. desert
volcano
ocean.
And some more words. Rainforest. A thick forest with a lot of rain. Continent.
One of the seven large areas of land on Earth. Temperature. How hot or cold something is.
Listen and say them. rainforest
continent
temperature.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: a very dry place with little rain?
Now some grammar: Superlatives.
Use the + -est (or the most + long adjective) to compare three or more things.
For example: Mount Everest is the highest mountain.
For example: It is the most famous waterfall.
Now listen, and read along. Earth's record breakers.
The hottest place: Some parts of the Sahara Desert in Africa can reach 50°C in summer.
Very few plants can grow there. The coldest place: Antarctica is the coldest continent.
In winter the temperature can fall below minus 80°C.
The wettest place: Some rainforests get rain almost every day.
One town in India gets more than eleven metres of rain a year!
The deepest place: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean is about eleven kilometres deep.
Only a few people have ever been to the bottom.
Another question. The video will stop. Where is the Sahara Desert?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like desert, volcano, ocean.
You practised superlatives. And you read Earth's record breakers.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

sections.title: A trip to the volcano

q.prompt: Which word means “a person who shows visitors around”?
q.reason: “guide” means a person who shows visitors around.

options.fb: “lava” means very hot liquid rock from a volcano.
“crater” means the hole at the top of a volcano.

captions: Hello, and welcome to Atomic English, Stage 4. In this lesson: A trip to the volcano.
Talk about plans with ‘going to’ and read a travel plan.
Here are some new words. Guide. A person who shows visitors around. Crater.
The hole at the top of a volcano. Lava. Very hot liquid rock from a volcano.
Listen and say them. guide
crater
lava.
And some more words. Erupt. When a volcano suddenly sends out lava and ash. Hike.
A long walk in the countryside. Explore. Travel around a place to find out about it.
Listen and say them. erupt
hike
explore.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: a person who shows visitors around?
Now some grammar: going to.
Use am / is / are + going to + verb for plans and for things we can see will happen.
For example: We are going to visit a volcano.
For example: Look at those clouds – it's going to rain.
Now listen, and read along. Our plan for Saturday.
On Saturday our class is going to visit Mount Fuego Park. Here is our plan.
8:00 We are going to meet at school and take the bus.
10:00 A guide is going to take us on a two-hour hike to the edge of the crater.
12:30 We are going to eat our lunch next to the old lava field.
2:00 We are going to explore the visitor centre and watch a film about how volcanoes erupt.
Remember: wear strong shoes, bring water and a hat!
Another question. The video will stop. Where is the class going?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like guide, crater, lava. You practised going to.
And you read Our plan for Saturday. Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
